newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hikes duty on Canadian hogs - U.S. industry.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hikes duty on Canadian hogs - U.S. industry.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department slightly raised countervailing duties on Canadian hogs imported to the U.S. between April 1991 and March 1994, U.S. National Pork Producers Council (NPPC) said Tuesday.
The final rates were lifted from preliminary rates set in late May and the department notified interested parties from both countries Monday, a spokeswoman for the council said.
Commerce officials said no public announcement had been made. The officials could not immediately confirm the new rates.
For hogs imported between April 1991 and March 1992, the rate rose to C$0.0601 per kg from the preliminary rate of C$0.0594 per kg, NPPC said.
For April 1992 to March 1993, the rate increased to C$0.0613 from C$0.0609 per kg. And for April 1993 to March 1994, the rate rose to C$0.0106 per kg from C$0.0099 per kg.
NPPC also said Commerce set a preliminary rate of C$0.0271 per kg for hogs imported between April 1994 and March 1995.
